title: Five Signs Your Suit Actually Fits
excerpt: Most fit problems have nothing to do with size on the tag. Here's what to check before you buy — or before your next fitting.
author: Lipek Fashion Team
body: Shoulder seams should sit exactly at the edge of your shoulder bone — not hanging past it, not pulling in. This is the single hardest thing to fix after the fact, which is why we check it first at every fitting.
The collar should sit flush against your shirt collar with no gap and no bunching. A gapping collar usually means the balance of the jacket is off, not just the size.
Sleeves should end where your wrist meets your hand, showing about half an inch of shirt cuff. Too long and the jacket looks borrowed; too short and it looks outgrown.
Trousers should break just once at the shoe, or sit clean with no break for a more modern cut — either is fine, as long as it's a choice and not an accident of length.

You should be able to fasten the top button of a two-button jacket without the fabric pulling into an X shape across the chest. That X is the most common sign of a jacket that's simply too small in the body.
